scenes.say: Hello, and welcome. In most companies, the attacker's goal is Domain Admins, the group that controls every Windows computer and account. They rarely get there with a single trick. They walk there, one permission at a time. Today you'll follow that walk from a helpdesk account to the top.

The setting. Nimbus Analytics in Hyderabad, Tuesday the tenth of November 2026. All times are UTC. A helpdesk worker, h.verma, fell for a phishing email, so the attacker has that account's password. The case folder has the company's identity data: which accounts are in which groups, and what each group is allowed to do.
First, who's who, and which accounts are protected by multi-factor sign-in.

scenes.after: Look at line two: Helpdesk can force a password change on svc-sql, inherited since 2023. And adm.k.nair has a session on app02, because a scheduled task runs as that account with a saved password.

scenes.say: Switch sides and think like the attacker. Defenders think in lists. Attackers think in graphs: from where I am, what can I reach? This short Python script follows the edges from h.verma, the phished account, to Domain-Admins, and writes the whole graph for Graphviz to draw.

scenes.after: A saved password on a machine you control counts as an edge, because an administrator can take it from memory or the registry.

Let's read the path, hop by hop. h.verma is a member of Helpdesk. Helpdesk has ForceChangePassword on svc-sql, a service account. That hop needs no new password: the attacker simply sets a new one. svc-sql is a member of Server-Admins. Server-Admins is admin on app02. adm.k.nair has a saved login on app02, and adm.k.nair is a member of Domain-Admins.

The red path: phished helpdesk account, reset a service account's password, admin on a server, take the saved Domain Admin login. Game over, and no exploit anywhere. Every arrow is a setting someone chose.

scenes.say: So which single change breaks the most paths? Removing the saved Domain Admin login from app02, by running that task as a low-privilege account, breaks every path that goes through it. Removing the old helpdesk reset right closes the door at the start. Do both.

scenes.type:
FIX, HOP BY HOP   Nimbus Analytics   10 Nov 2026 (UTC)
Hop 1  Helpdesk can reset svc-sql           remove the old reset right on the Service Accounts folder
Hop 4  adm.k.nair's saved login on app02    run Nightly KPI export as a low-privilege account
Both together close every path to Domain-Admins that goes through app02.

scenes.say: That was one step from Seminar 7, Identity from both sides: AD, Entra and cloud IAM. The full seminar has a longer video, every step at three levels, a graded hand-in that I mark myself, and a certificate at the end. The links are on your screen.

To recap. Attackers think in graphs, not lists. Follow each permission one hop at a time, and remember that a saved password is an edge. Then fix the hop that breaks the most paths. Thank you for watching.
